transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-03-21
- Start: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 52m
- Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Marigold Head of Security), Sofia Martinez (Marigold CTO), Devon Lee (Marigold Platform Eng)

Summary (auto):
Quick security posture intake focused on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML and RBAC model, KMS/BYOK options, audit log retention, and deployment choices (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Agreed to share SOC2 Type II, set up test VPC for benchmarks, SE to propose pilot sizing and pricing.

Topics:
- Compliance baseline (SOC2/ISO)
- Identity & access (SSO, SAML, SCIM, RBAC)
- Encryption & key management (BYOK, HSM, envelope encryption)
- Audit logs & retention windows
- Deployment topology (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC/on-prem)
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on this account, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sofia Martinez: Hey Ethan, hi Priya. Doing well. Thanks for taking the time.
[00:09] Liam O'Connor: Afternoon. We're hoping to get through our security checklist so we know if Redwood fits our production constraints.
[00:14] Priya Rao: Great, we'll run through SOC2/ISO coverage, identity, keys, logs, and then deployment options — and we can mark any follow-ups.
[00:20] Devon Lee: Quick note, I'm most interested in the network layout and the KV cache implications on latency, but security first.
[00:26] Ethan Park: Makes sense. Liam, can you share your high-level constraints? I know Marigold is PCI-adjacent and doing EU expansion so data residency matters?
[00:33] Liam O'Connor: Yeah so two main things: one is auditability for payments-adjacent flows — auditors want seven years of logs in some cases — and two is that some customer data must remain in EU regions. Also SSO is required for vendor tools, SAML-based, with SCIM provisioning ideally.
[00:47] Priya Rao: Understood. On SOC2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted service and our org processes, and we also maintain ISO 27001 for the control set of our control plane — I will share the relevant artifacts. Note: the SOC2 scope covers hosted API and control plane, whereas Dedicated and Private have a different responsibilities split — we'll call that out.
[01:06] Sofia Martinez: Can you clarify that split? Specifically what falls into customer responsibility vs Redwood for Dedicated and Private?
[01:12] Priya Rao: Sure. For Dedicated, Redwood manages the inference runtime and the node-level security — we own the application and runtime patches, the GPU substrate, and the ingestion path for the models. Customers are responsible for network-level isolation and their own VPC networking rules and cloud IAM when using a Dedicated VPC link. For Private/on-prem, the customer is responsible for the full infra stack — Redwood's control plane can be configured to be customer-managed or we can operate within a restricted management channel.
[01:36] Liam O'Connor: Ok so for Dedicated we still need to provide our own encryption keys? We want BYOK and an HSM-backed KMS.
[01:43] Priya Rao: We support BYOK for both Dedicated and Private. For Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and a KMS integration (customer-managed keys) as an enterprise option. For Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we also support HSM-backed keys via partner HSMs.
[02:02] Devon Lee: How does tokenization/kv cache work with BYOK? Any risk of keys in memory or persisted caches?
[02:08] Priya Rao: Great question. The runtime keeps model KV cache in process memory — we never persist plaintext keys to disk. Envelope keys are used to encrypt persisted artifacts; the keys themselves never leave the KMS; we hold wrapped keys for faster startup but they are hardware-isolated. That said, we can arrange an architecture where the decryption happens inside a customer-controlled subnet or Private deployment so the unwrapped keys never transit Redwood-managed control planes.
[02:33] Ethan Park: There's sometimes confusion — K V cache gets transcribed as K V cash — transcription aside, the important bit is the KV material isn't storing customer cleartext PII.
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: That helps. About SSO — we use Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM user provisioning. We need RBAC to match our internal roles and also audit trails for admin actions.
[02:52] Priya Rao: Redwood supports SAML SSO via IdP integration and SCIM for provisioning. For RBAC we have role templates and can add custom roles; admin actions like model promotion, rollback, and key rotations are all logged in the audit trail. You can also restrict model access via per-team tokens.
[03:08] Sofia Martinez: Is there fine-grained RBAC for who can call the inference endpoints vs who can deploy models?
[03:13] Priya Rao: Yes, we separate control plane actions (deploy, rollout, config) from data plane inference calls. Tokens for inference can be scoped per-model and per-route, and the Console supports token-level permissions. We'll show RBAC examples in the follow-up.
[03:25] Devon Lee: Audit logs — retention and format? We need syslog forwarding into our SIEM and immutable logs for compliance.
[03:31] Priya Rao: We can stream audit events to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 logs with encryption. Retention default is 90 days in Redwood Console for hosted, but for enterprise we can configure longer retention or export to customer-owned buckets for archival. We also support WORM-like controls via the customer's cloud object controls.
[03:51] Liam O'Connor: You mentioned default 90 days — auditors want seven years for certain payment traces. Can Redwood support seven-year archival?
[03:58] Priya Rao: Yes — by exporting logs to customer-managed S3/GCS and using your archival lifecycle rules you can meet seven-year retention. We will include a sample log export config.
[04:07] Ethan Park: Also note that for Private/on-prem deployments, all logs can be kept entirely within your network, so Redwood never sees the audit log content unless you opt to share it.
[04:15] Sofia Martinez: Good. Another point: model artifacts and customer prompts — do you store prompts, and what's the retention? We are trying to avoid storing full PII in prompts.
[04:24] Priya Rao: By default Redwood retains request/response metadata for troubleshooting short-term; full request/response storage is opt-in and can be disabled. For Dedicated and Private you can elect to disable request storage entirely. We'll share the exact flags. Best practice is to scrub PII before sending but we also support pre-ingest redaction and tokenization.
[04:41] Devon Lee: On data residency: can we pin Dedicated nodes to eu-west-1 and ensure failover stays in EU?
[04:46] Priya Rao: Yes — routing policies allow regional pinning. For high availability we support multi-AZ within the same region. Cross-region failover can be disabled to comply with residency constraints.
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: About penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure — what's Redwood's stance and do we get permission to run scans?
[05:02] Priya Rao: We have a vulnerability disclosure policy and allow customer-led pen tests on Dedicated and Private with a sign-off. Hosted customers have a standard set of allowed tests — we'll share the policy.
[05:12] Sofia Martinez: Can you talk about network ingress/egress — egress firewalling, private endpoints, and whether Dedicated requires a direct connect or can use peering?
[05:20] Priya Rao: Dedicated supports VPC peering, PrivateLink/Private Service Connect depending on cloud provider, and can be configured to only accept traffic from your VPC CIDR. We also support egress controls to block outbound internet for model downloads if you want self-hosted model bits.
[05:36] Devon Lee: Is there support for image/model signing so we can verify code provenance?
[05:39] Priya Rao: Yes, model signing and attestations are part of our model onboarding pipeline for enterprise customers. We can store signatures in an attestations log or integrate with your supply chain tools.
[05:48] Ethan Park: Quick procurement note — procurement/legal will want a data processing addendum and a security questionnaire filled out. We'll deliver our standard DPA and completed Pentera vendor form as part of the follow-up.
[05:58] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. One more: encryption at rest for ephemeral artifacts and swap files on GPU nodes — how is that handled?
[06:05] Priya Rao: All node disks are encrypted at rest with provider-managed or customer-managed keys. Swap or ephemeral caches are in-memory where possible; any persisted temp state is encrypted with envelope keys. We can produce a diagram of the key lifecycle.
[06:18] Sofia Martinez: About certifications: is your SOC2 Type II scoped for the entire Redwood platform or limited to the hosted control plane?
[06:25] Priya Rao: The SOC2 Type II covers Redwood's hosted service and our control plane processes. For Dedicated and Private the control plane pieces we operate are included, but responsibilities shift — we'll annotate the report with the control boundaries.
[06:38] Devon Lee: For BYOK, rotation cadence — can we rotate keys monthly without downtime?
[06:43] Priya Rao: Key rotation is designed to be seamless. We support key versioning and rotation patterns that allow zero-downtime rotations for wrapped keys. For deep HSM rotations there is a short rewrap window but we bake it into the runtime to avoid user-facing downtime.
[06:58] Ethan Park: Want to surface a typical architecture we see for retail customers — they pick Dedicated with private VPC peering, BYOK via AWS KMS with HSM billing, and export logs to their S3 bucket for archival. That combination meets residency and audit requirements with minimal latency hit.
[07:17] Liam O'Connor: That sounds like the direction we lean. How about costs — Dedicated pilot sizing for our peak of ~100 concurrent inference sessions per second?
[07:26] Priya Rao: We'll need a short benchmark to translate concurrent sessions to GPU vram/throughput; we typically size by peak tokens-per-second and model family. For that we can provision a benchmark cluster in a test VPC and run your representative load.
[07:39] Sofia Martinez: Can Redwood's Console provide token-level billing and mapping to team owners for cost allocation?
[07:44] Priya Rao: Yes — Console exposes token-level cost attribution, per-route/model breakdowns and chargeback tags. You can ingest that into your internal billing system.
[07:54] Devon Lee: Will the benchmark include evals on quantized models — we may want to use int8 to save cost. Any security impacts?
[07:59] Priya Rao: Quantization is purely model runtime and doesn't change the data flow security posture. The key is ensuring model artifacts are verified. Quantized artifacts can be treated the same for signing and KMS controls.
[08:10] Liam O'Connor: Procurement timeline — we aim to be in pilot by May 15. Is that realistic?
[08:15] Ethan Park: Yes, that's feasible if we get the SOW and pilot sizing agreed in two weeks. We'll target a week to send docs and a week to finalize procurement.
[08:23] Priya Rao: I'll note that we need their retention policy and PII flows to complete the security plan.
[08:28] Ethan Park: Ok quick sanity check — anything we missed?
[08:31] Liam O'Connor: Rollback/fallback policy if a model misbehaves in production — can we auto-fallback to a safe stub or earlier model?
[08:38] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to a pinned model or lower-tier variant if latency or error thresholds are exceeded. Those rollouts are auditable.
[08:48] Sofia Martinez: Can we lock down model deployments to only specific users via RBAC?
[08:52] Priya Rao: Yes — tie deployments to roles and require two-person approval for production deploys if you want. We can enforce that via the Console.
[08:59] Devon Lee: Anything about supply chain — can we request a SBOM for delivery artifacts?
[09:03] Priya Rao: We can provide SBOMs for the container images and the runtime. For models, we provide audit trails and signing attestations.
[09:11] Ethan Park: Cool. I'll stop the list here and open the floor for any deeper technical questions.
[09:15] Devon Lee: One: network egress — when models call out for external tool connectors, does Redwood allow an egress allowlist so we only permit certain external endpoints?
[09:23] Priya Rao: We support egress allowlist and can also route those calls through your NAT so you can inspect outbound. For Hosted customers, egress is restricted by default and we can provide an approvals path for connector endpoints.
[09:36] Liam O'Connor: Two: for incident response, will we get a timeline and an incident log?
[09:40] Priya Rao: We publish incident timelines for any service-level incident, and enterprise customers get a post-incident report. We also provide a dedicated Slack channel or PagerDuty integration for higher tiers.
[09:50] Sofia Martinez: Three: encryption in motion — TLS, mutual TLS?
[09:54] Priya Rao: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; for higher assurance we support mTLS for service-to-service and can present client certs for dedicated peered links.
[10:03] Ethan Park: We're at about ten minutes into our chat — we've covered a lot but we'll keep going through a few customer scenarios.
[10:09] Devon Lee: Scenario A: we want private inference for high-value PII processing in our environment, but keep the rest of our org on Hosted — can Redwood support hybrid?
[10:18] Priya Rao: Absolutely. We've done hybrid deployments where certain clients route to Private clusters while others use Hosted. Routing policies can be per-tenant, per-route or by region.
[10:28] Liam O'Connor: Any additional audit artifacts for hybrid?
[10:31] Priya Rao: We correlate telemetry across clusters and can provide combined audit views if you want Redwood-managed aggregation; alternatively you can keep them segregated in your logging.
[10:41] Sofia Martinez: Let's talk about legal — can Redwood sign an addendum for data residency and subprocessing?
[10:46] Ethan Park: We have standard DPA and subprocessor lists; for stricter terms we go through our legal review but it's typically doable for enterprise contracts.
[10:54] Liam O'Connor: For the SOC2 docs you mentioned, will you annotate which controls map to client obligations?
[10:59] Priya Rao: Yes, we'll provide a control matrix mapping Redwood controls to customer responsibilities for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[11:07] Ethan Park: Great. Anything else urgent?
[11:10] Liam O'Connor: One small one — are API keys in Console able to be rotated automatically?
[11:15] Priya Rao: Yes, API keys support rotation, expiration and can be scoped. Also you can require MFA for Console admin users.
[11:22] Devon Lee: Also do you have a retention config for model artifact versions? We want to keep just the last three production models.
[11:27] Priya Rao: You can set artifact retention and number of versions per-namespace; we can set defaults at org-level.
[11:33] Sofia Martinez: Okay if we stop here — this was super helpful.
[11:36] Ethan Park: Quick recap of next steps — Priya will send SOC2 and ISO docs, plus audit log sample; we'll provision test VPC for benchmarks; Ethan will send pilot pricing. We'll get a follow-up scheduled.
[11:47] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Thanks both.
[11:50] Priya Rao: Thanks, we'll get those out this week.
[11:53] Ethan Park: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
